authorization: User requested all 75 whole practice questions from Trigonometry 4B: Graphs, Equations and the Ambiguous Case; teaching content excluded.
method: Ordinary promotion in isolated staging, verified once and published through a checked transaction.

classification.difficultyReason: Parts a to c are routine exact values, with a negative angle converted to a coterminal one. The hardest demand is part d, where the student must generalise from three paired examples to the odd/even identities sin(-θ) = -sin θ, cos(-θ) = cos θ and tan(-θ) = -tan θ. This is a modest pattern-spotting and representation step, and the examples provide the scaffolding. Part e then applies the result to simplify an expression. This is above straight recall of exact values but well below non-trivial reframing.

classification.difficultyReason: Nine direct exact values that include negative angles and one angle above 360°. This is less coterminal reduction than p40-q9.

questions.mappingNote: trig-ratios-quadrant-forms is the primary skill recorded on this master question; its audit-v2 review is current for this content.

classification.difficultyReason: The student reads three points on the unit circle diagram and uses the marked acute reference angle (30°, 45°, 60°) directly. The (±cos A, ±sin A) form is supplied, so the main decisions are the quadrant of each point, the signs that follow, and recalling the exact values. This is more demanding than p37-q1, which reads values straight from a labelled circle, and than the single-step p68-q7. It is easier than p40-q8, which has no ± scaffold and includes a negative-angle coterminal case and non-unit radii. It is also easier than p39-q5, where the reference angle must be found from an unmarked angle. There is no new insight and no directed-angle ambiguity, unlike p41-q10.

classification.difficultyReason: Two short proofs, each needing two or three reduction identities (supplementary, complementary and 180°+θ), then a simplification using tan=sin/cos. It is lighter than p42-q12, which has four reductions in one proof. Each step is routine and the identities are the taught ones, so it is a routine linked procedure with no unsignposted insight.

classification.difficultyReason: Part a needs rearrangement to cos θ = 1/2, then a reference angle and the Q1/Q4 solutions. Part b uses the boundary value cos θ = -1, which has a single solution. Part c is heavily scaffolded: the student splits the product and reuses the answers from a and b. The hardest demand is a routine two-quadrant trig solve, below the multi-stage reasoning in p68-q7.

It is harder than p62-q7 (single-step equation from the gradient) and easier than the multi-part p63-q10.
